title: I’m using AI to turn 10+ years of investing experience into a live quantitative system — and testing it with real money
author: US-Leaders-Quant
selftext:
I’ve spent more than 10 years investing in U.S. stocks.

Over that time, I’ve developed my own way of thinking about markets, companies, momentum, risk, position selection, and when to stay out of the market.

For years, those ideas mostly lived in my head.

I always wanted to turn them into a systematic investment process, but there was a practical problem:

**I didn’t really have the tools to do it well.**

That changed with AI.

I’m not using AI to tell me what stocks to buy.

The investment philosophy is mine. The ideas are mine. The system I’m building is based on principles I’ve developed through years of investing.

What AI has given me is something I didn’t have before:

**the ability to turn those ideas into a systematic, quantitative process.**

So now I’m finally putting the idea to the test.

The system is running live.

Instead of showing a backtest and telling you how well it would have worked, I want to see what happens in the real market.

I’m going to publish my trading activity as it happens:

* When an order is submitted
* When it gets filled
* When an order is cancelled
* What positions are eventually closed at
* The resulting gains, losses and drawdowns

I’m deliberately not going to publish the actual strategy rules or parameters. If there is something valuable in the system, I don't think giving away the mechanics would make much sense.

But I do want the **track record to be transparent**.

If I make a good trade, it will be there.

If I make a bad trade, it will be there too.

If I go weeks without trading, that will be there as well.

And importantly, I’m publishing orders as they happen rather than reconstructing trades afterward from historical prices.

The question I’m really interested in is not:

**“Can AI pick stocks?”**

It’s:

**“Can an investment philosophy developed over many years be translated into a systematic process that can actually survive real-time markets?”**

I don't know the answer yet.

That’s exactly why I’m running the experiment.

For people here who work with AI or systematic trading: has anyone else gone through the transition from discretionary investment ideas to a live systematic process?

What did you learn that you wish you knew before going live?

comments.author: profittoinvest
comments.body:
One thing I’d strongly recommend is keeping the original live version unchanged for a while, even when you spot things you want to improve. If you want to test a change, make a copy and test that separately. Otherwise it becomes very hard to tell whether the original idea actually had an edge.

Also compare the live trades with your historical/backtest expectations over exactly the same period. Look at missed trades, entry/exit differences, fees, slippage, capital constraints and drawdowns — not just total return. Even a few skipped or differently filled trades can make the live equity path diverge surprisingly quickly.

The most useful thing we learned was that the real question isn’t only “does it make money?”, but “does the live behaviour match what the research said should happen?” That takes months, not days.

Your approach of publishing the good trades, bad trades and drawdowns as they happen is probably the right way to find out.

You have a long road ahead of you, but the challenge is definitely worth taking on. If you have the knowledge, a proven method of your own, and the confidence that it holds a market advantage, you should certainly be able to turn it into a solid algorithmic system.
